summary: A 1936 Art Deco crib lighthouse in the Grays Reef Passage near the Straits of Mackinac, replacing a steam lightship that marked the reef from 1891.

access.note: Privately owned; tower closed. Best seen from a boat or the air.

notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination PDF is not digitised (22 KB placeholder). Keeper roster is the USLHS archive's (NARA registers); not confirmed against a primary record. Roster begins 1936 though the station commissioned 1937. LighthouseFriends dates the lightship's electric light to 1930; Bulletin 1925 lists acetylene to electric incandescent, so the date is unresolved. LighthouseFriends says the ships were placed 24 Oct 1891; the Light-House Board lists lights/whistle from 22 Oct 1891. LighthouseFriends is the only source for the 1965 collision, 1976 automation and the 2016 auction; the 1966 newspaper article and 1976 Record-Eagle it lists were not read. The 1899 report's OCR gives '189S' for the departure year, read as December 1898 from context. Page numbers for Light-House Board reports are scan pages. Angus H. Phillips appears as a lightship engineer in 1916 and a lighthouse keeper in 1939-40: not linked. Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy, Wikipedia (LV-57 article) not used. Fact-check 2026-10-27: footnotes 2 and 3 are the FY1891 report (bound with FY1892 in annualreportlig03statgoog; FY1892 starts at scan p.326), relabelled; Bulletin 1929 lightning item is PDF p.27. The 82 ft in the 1936 Bulletin is in a damaged OCR column; the USLHS record's 82 ft height of light corroborates it. Bulletin 1929 calls No. 103 a relief ship against LighthouseFriends' 1923 replacement claim; stated in the story.
